newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong dlr bonds take a hit on currency worries. [CORRECTED 12:38 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong dlr bonds take a hit on currency worries. [CORRECTED 12:38 GMT]

text.p: Hong Kong dollar bonds suffered from heavy selling amid fears that the Hong Kong dollar could come under attack from speculators, traders said on Friday.
"We saw some unloading on Hong Kong dollar floating rate paper," said a trader at a European investment bank.
Hong Kong dollar spot rates slipped to HK$7.7490/7.7500 per U.S. dollar from about HK$7.7465/75 on Thursday and forward rates soared.
Overnight interest rates also jumped, at one point brushing against 8.00 percent, about 150 basis points higher than on Thursday.

Bankers said that Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp's three-year floating rate certificate of deposit (corrects from "floating rate note") issue widened to over 30 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate from the 27 basis points it paid when it was launched two weeks ago.
Hong Kong government bonds of shorter maturity also took a hit, and the yield spread between Hong Kong Exchange Fund Notes and U.S. Treasuries widened.
By midafternoon, spreads between Hong Kong and U.S. dollar government debt ballooned by 33 basis points in the two-year maturity and 48 basis points in the three-month maturity.
Bankers said they expected the weakness in the Hong Kong dollar bonds to be short-lived.
"I would expect the Hong Kong dollar bonds will soon consolidate in the coming one to two weeks," a trader at a Japanese investment bank said.
